title: Width associated with a kind
statement: Let $\kappa$ be a type, let $m$ and $w$ be natural numbers, and let $F$ assign a Boolean list to each pair consisting of an element of $\kappa$ and a Boolean list. For each $\kappa_0\in\kappa$, define its kind width to be the embedding width of the kind gadgets determined by $m$, $w$, $F$, and $\kappa_0$.
caveat: The snippet relies on the upstream notions of kind gadgets and embedding width, whose definitions are not included in the supplied payload.
